question: Non-selective monoamine oxidase inhibitors (e.g., phenelzine) are safe to co-prescribe with levodopa/carbidopa in Parkinson's disease patients who also have treatment-resistant depression.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Non-selective MAO inhibitors are ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED with levodopa. The combination risks life-threatening hypertensive crisis through excessive catecholamine accumulation. This is one of the 'two most dangerous drug interactions in PD pharmacotherapy' that every clinician must know. Selective MAO-B inhibitors (selegiline, rasagiline) are safe and beneficial adjuncts in PD.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct that this is FALSE. Co-administration of non-selective MAO inhibitors with levodopa is CONTRAINDICATED due to risk of hypertensive crisis. Non-selective MAOIs block peripheral and central catecholamine breakdown; combined with levodopa-derived dopamine and noradrenaline, this produces a dangerous catecholamine surge. Only selective MAO-B inhibitors (selegiline, rasagiline, safinamide) are used therapeutically in PD — and even these require caution with concurrent serotonergic agents.
